title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 21: Leave Room for the Bees

planning.voiceReason: A mistaken intervention threatens the garden and calls for restraint.
planning.earlyCare: Jon wants children to have a safe path and stops to straighten a fallen garden sign.
planning.desire: Make the teaching garden safe for children.
planning.obstacle: Jon mistakes a nest near the old route for an enemy to remove.
planning.dramaticChange: Jon learns that protection can mean leaving space and redirecting people.
planning.sourceBoundary: The crew clears the centre's neglected teaching garden. Jon mistakes a nest near the path for an enemy to remove. A knowledgeable gardener redirects the group before anyone rushes at it or strikes the insects. They cordon off the area and work on a safe section, learning why flowers and pollinators matter to the community.
sceneActivities: Jon approaches a closed garden path, stops well back from the nest, lowers his hands and helps mark an alternate route. A trained specialist manages the isolated area offstage. No handling or striking bees.

actingSignature.Jonathan: Plain practical questions; open hand at a boundary, quiet attention afterward.
actingSignature.An: Specific limits and short questions; supported seated rest while reviewing, no assumed healing.
actingSignature.Min: Urgent explanations soften into admitting uncertainty; rests attentive when corrected.
actingSignature.Mother: Concrete requests and accurate accounting; no presumed forgiveness or renewed station shift.
actingSignature.Sela: Patient concrete questions; does not reach for private report. Quiet open posture and attentive gaze.
actingSignature.Ivo: Begins with explanations and permissions; shifts to asking his son. Guarded hands, then release into attentive rest.
actingSignature.Edda: Firm stop and clear safety boundary; calm practical answers while Jonathan lowers his hand.

planning.listenerTurn: Gardener Edda tells Jon the bees are not attacking; listener Jon; he lowers his hand and waits.
planning.payoff: A safe garden route and appropriate specialist care protect both people and pollinators; a local grower's donation supports the opening-day stall.
planning.freshQuestion: Min and a resident cook run a small food stall to fund approved centre supplies. Jon imagines a grand feast, then discovers that prices, portions and ordinary soup matter more. A customer challenges an exaggerated honey advertisement; the cook removes its weight-loss and calming claims. They choose a shared meal and transparent accounts over prestige.

teaser.moment: Jon stands beyond a garden barrier and quietly lowers his open hand, watching a bee visit flowers while leaving space.

continuation.end: Edda, the garden keeper, helps Jonathan replace the urge to attack with patient protection. A qualified specialist inspects the nest area; the old path is isolated pending appropriate management and an alternate path is checked safe. Edda’s grower relative promises seedlings for the opening stall; this is a promise, not delivered stock. No station water is used. Repairs and the centre reopening remain pending.
